rounds.gap: critic 1: Unticking and re-ticking an OLD occurrence after the series has ended forks it. SEED (the recur-check 'ends after 3' seed): clock 2026-03-10 09:00 America/New_York, things-todos=[{id:'t1',title:'Physio exercises',when:'2026-03-11',repeat:{mode:'completion',every:1,unit:'day',ends:{after:3}}}], route #/upcoming. STEPS: (1) click the open row's checkbox 3 times -> t1 (occ1), occ2, occ3 all completed, none open (correct). (2) #/logbook: click t1's checkbox (untick). (3) #/upcoming: click t1's checkbox (tick again). Same with keyboard: in the Logbook click t1's label to select it and press Cmd/Ctrl+K twice. EXPECTED: untick+retick is a no-op: 3 to-dos, 0 open. Contract: 'ends.after is the total number of occurrences in the series, counting the first'; the Logbook reopen must not fork the series (on a live series the engine does this right: the reopened one comes back as a one-off and re-ticking spawns nothing). ACTUAL (localStorage): 4 to-dos in series t1: t1 [x] nextId->new, a NEW open 'Physio exercises' occurrence:2 dated 2026-03-11, plus the old occ2 [x] and occ3 [x]. So two occurrence-2 to-dos, the series has come back to life, and ends.after is exceeded (it can reach 5). Same with the 'ends on' seed (Take antibiotics, schedule daily from 2026-03-10, ends.on 2026-03-12): after completing Mar 10/11/12, untick Mar 10 in the Logbook and re-tick it in Today. That gives a second 2026-03-11 occurrence (open) next to the completed Mar 11 one. The same revival also happens after the open occurrence is deleted, which the contract says ends the series. CAUSE: store.js reopen() strips the rule only when another OPEN repeating occurrence exists (line 336). An ended series has none, so t1 keeps its repeat with occurrence 1, and complete() spawns occ 2 again without seeing that t1's successor (nextId) already exists as a completed to-do. Reproduced 2 of 2 from clean start. Not caught by recur-check, whose invariant only counts open repeating to-dos.  ·  critic 3: Seed (clock Tue 2026-03-10 09:00 America/New_York): one to-do t1 'Pay rent' {when:'2026-03-10', project:'p_house', repeat:{mode:'schedule',every:1,unit:'month'}}. Two tabs (same context, same localStorage) both on #/project/p_house. Steps: (1) tab A ticks the 'Pay rent' row checkbox, creating the next occurrence N (when 2026-04-10). (2) Tab A double-clicks N to open its card and types nothing. (3) Tab B double-clicks N, presses End, types ' to landlord', presses Enter. Storage now has N 'Pay rent to landlord'. (4) Tab A clicks empty space; pressing Escape does the same. (5) Tab A unticks t1 with its row checkbox. Expected: tab A typed nothing, so the rename stays. CONTRACT: 'a typed title makes a next occurrence edited', and unticking takes back the occurrence only 'as long as that one is still open and unedited', so N should stay and t1 should reopen as a one-off. That is exactly what the control run (the same steps without tab A's card open) gives: t1 [ ] 'Pay rent' with no rule, and N [ ] 'Pay rent to landlord' repeating. Actual (2/2 clean runs, both close paths): at step 4, tab A's close() writes back the title it has held in its field since the card mounted (detail.js close: edit.value !== t.title -> updateTodo), so N becomes 'Pay rent' again. N's fingerprint then matches its spawnKey, so at step 5 reopen() drops N. Final storage is [t1 [ ] 'Pay rent', repeating] only, the tab B rows after reload are ['Pay rent'], and ' to landlord' is nowhere. The rename typed in tab B is lost, and the occurrence it was typed into is then deleted. No page errors. The storage listener reloads state, but sync() never refreshes the card's title field, so any close of a stale card silently overwrites the other tab. STEPS: (1) tick 'Water plants' with its row checkbox -> t1 [x], next occurrence N (2026-03-13) open in House. (2) Click the 'Buy milk' row once (it becomes selected, li.selected). (3) Click the toolbar Complete All (label.tool[for=toggle-all]); it read unchecked before the click. EXPECTED: Complete All completes every to-do in the list (CONTRACT: the engine works 'through every completion path: the row checkbox, the card checkbox, Complete All, Cmd/Ctrl+K and the phone menu'; Complete All 'spawns one next occurrence per repeating to-do'), so Buy milk [x], N [x] plus one new occurrence, and Complete All reads checked. CAUSE: the label's synthetic click on the hidden #toggle-all bubbles to the scroller's deselect-on-empty-click listener (view.js ~437); its setUI re-render writes store.allCompleted() back into #toggle-all (view.js:247) before the change event, so setCompleted() receives the old state inverted. critic 3: In Upcoming, where every next occurrence lands, the open card of an occurrence closes by itself when its row moves, even though the to-do never leaves the list. What the person types next is lost, and if the title field is empty at that moment the occurrence is deleted.

SEED: desktop 1200x800, America/New_York, clock Tue 2026-03-10 09:00, lists as in recur-check (project p_house). Todos: t0 'Dentist' {when:'2026-03-13', project:'p_house'} and t1 'Change water filter' {when:'2026-03-20', project:'p_house', repeat:{mode:'completion',every:1,unit:'week'}}.

STEPS (#/upcoming, one tab, repeat-engine path):
1. Double-click the t1 row to open its card.
2. Click the notes and type 'Used the spare cartridge'.
3. Press Cmd+K. It is done early, and the next occurrence lands on Tue Mar 17, in a section above it. The card stays open with focus in the notes.
4. Press Cmd+K again to undo. The next occurrence is taken back.
5. Keep typing 'Next-time-buy-two'.

EXPECTED: t1 is still in Upcoming, so its card stays open with focus in the notes and the text goes there, as it does with the same steps in #/project/p_house. CONTRACT: 'Cmd/Ctrl+K in the open card works wherever its focus is ... and acts on the card's to-do, like its checkbox. A card or selection whose to-do leaves the list on screen ... closes or is dropped with it'. Also 'Escape in the title still restores the old one, unless completing or reopening from the card has already committed it', which means the card is still open after reopening from it. This counts as a break because something the user typed is lost.

ACTUAL (2/2 clean runs, no page errors): after the second Cmd+K the card is closed and focus is on BODY. The typed text goes into Quick Find (qf-input = 'Next-time-buy-two'). Stored t1.notes = 'Used the spare cartridge', so the typed text is lost. Control in #/project/p_house: the card stays open and notes = 'Used the spare cartridgeNext-time-buy-two'.

SAME CAUSE, MORE COMMON TRIGGER: rescheduling an occurrence from its open card in Upcoming. Seed t1 'Water plants' {when:'2026-03-12', weekly schedule}. Double-click it, type ' and ferns', click the When chip, type 'mon' and press Enter. The picker hands focus back to the title. Then type ' on the balcony'. The card has already closed. The space opens the composer, so new-todo = 'on the balcony' (Enter would add it as a stray to-do), and the title stays 'Water plants and ferns'. Moving an occurrence to This Evening from its card in Today does the same.

WORST CASE: clear the title to retype it (Cmd+A, Backspace), then reschedule from the When chip. The card closes by itself, close() finds an empty title, and t1 is deleted with its notes, checklist and rule. The series is gone. In the project-view control the card stays open and t1 is kept.

CAUSE: rows.js reconcile() re-inserts the editing li with insertBefore when a section before it goes away or the row changes date section. A MutationObserver trace shows the li removed and re-added. The detached field loses focus, and detail.js's focusout handler then calls close(), which removes a to-do whose title field is empty.
